raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Assessing growth potential and strategy in the Financing Business",
  "main_topics": ["Financing Business growth", "Fixed Income Financing", "Prime business", "Client targeting", "Risk management", "Business model", "Technology integration", "Market positioning", "Margin trade-off", "Future growth prospects"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "I wanted to ask about the Financing Business, please. I mean, that's been working well for you. As Dan said earlier, you've been focused on the largest of the hedge funds. But, from what we can see, and I think disclosure across the industry isn't very good here, but from what we can see, your penetration into those very largest hedge funds is now approaching the kind of top three Financing firms to the big US banks. But where you have less penetration is in kind of the next rung down. Is there still a lot more scope, you think to increase penetration further and really kind of catch up or maybe even overtake the biggest players in the industry among that top group of hedge funds? Or are you going to have to start focusing more on the next rungs down?",
  "answer_quote": "Our Financing business is working well and remember this comes in two parts. So, our Fixed Income Financing business, very much embedded in the heritage of Barclays and Lehman before it. It is typically number one or two in the market. So very, very well-established business. What we've been doing is growing Prime alongside that. We've gone from typically number seven or eight to joint number five. So, we've clearly made some progress there. As you note, our targeting has been with the larger of the hedge funds, that's deliberate, and it reflects both our business model and our view of risk. So by business model, what I mean is we run our Financing business as an integrated business. So Fixed Income Financing and Prime are run under a single leadership. So when we approach a client, that's how we approach them, not as two individual businesses. We also run our technology that way. So, as we're looking at those clients, we look across their business in its totality, and we believe that gives us a better perspective of their risk. That lends itself to the largest global multi-strategy type funds, so that's really why you see that approach. But also, in terms of our own risk positioning, we do believe that, again, the first step in risk management is through the careful selection of clients, and therefore we choose to work with the larger, more capitalised, more liquid clients in the industry. That's really where we prefer to operate. That may mean that we give up a little margin along the way, but that certainly is a risk matter where we would want to operate. So, it's a deliberate strategy. So, from our perspective, we would want to grow as they do. Clearly, we do feel there's more for us to do there. Thank you so much. Really appreciate you coming in again on a very busy day in the market. So, appreciate your time and questions, particularly on Best Egg. We will see you on the 10th of February, if not before. Thank you very much."
}
